title: Phishing attacks - bank liability under RBI guidelines
p1:
A fake SMS. A copied bank logo. One careless click. Can the bank still be responsible for your lost money?

Many customers assume that once a fraud happens, the loss is automatically theirs. But RBI guidelines have a different approach.
p2:
A surprising fact: customers may not always have to bear the entire loss in an online banking fraud.

If an unauthorized transaction happens and the customer informs the bank quickly, the customer's liability can be limited or even zero in certain situations, especially when the customer was not at fault.
p3:
RBI's framework focuses on who was responsible for the breach. Banks are expected to have systems to protect customers and respond to fraud reports. However, customers must also act carefully by avoiding suspicious links, sharing OTPs, or revealing banking details.

The practical lesson: report phishing-related transactions immediately. The speed of your response can directly impact your financial liability.
conclusion: Have you ever received a suspicious bank message or phishing link? Do you think customers know enough about their rights after online fraud?
